sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Java OOP interview questions are the single most common opener in any backend interview, from junior to staff. This page is dedicated to object-oriented design in Java — the four pillars (encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction), access modifiers, abstract classes vs interfaces, composition vs inheritance, and the SOLID principles applied to real Java code. Expect questions that test conceptual depth ("explain Liskov substitution with an example") as well as design judgement ("would you use an abstract class or an interface here, and why?"). Every answer comes with a short code snippet, the trade-off the interviewer is listening for, and the follow-up they are likely to ask next.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Four pillars + one principle set:

- **Encapsulation** — package-private + getters; minimise mutability.
- **Inheritance** — *IS-A*; in Java, classes single, interfaces many.
- **Polymorphism** — compile-time (overloading) vs runtime (overriding); only the latter dispatches dynamically.
- **Abstraction** — `abstract class` for partial impl, `interface` for capability/contract.
- **SOLID** — five orthogonal principles; cite them by name (S/O/L/I/D).

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Oop principles** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Composition over inheritance** — quote it, then defend it with one concrete example.
- **Abstract class vs interface in Java 8+** — both can have method bodies; use abstract for **state**, interface for **capability**.
- **Liskov** in code — substitution must hold without surprise (no narrower exceptions, no stricter preconditions).
- **`equals` symmetry / transitivity** — break it and you'll be asked to find the bug.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd model this as <abstraction> + <implementation>, leaning on <interface | abstract class> because <reason rooted in cohesion / state / capability>. The SOLID principle most stressed here is <S/O/L/I/D> — the alternative would have been <inheritance | composition>, but it would have broken <contract / testability>."*
